    • Queries navigation

      • D1 - Show only the title and year for every movie to build a compact catalog view.
      • D2 - List every movie title in the database to produce an alphabetical film list.
      • D3 - Find movie IDs for films that have never received any awards.
      • D4 - Return movies directed by Christopher Nolan.
      • D5 - Find actors who have appeared in every genre (Universal Quantification).
      • D6 - Show the names of actors found in the previous query (D5) to verify the results.
      • D7 - Show movies with their directors, keeping only films released after 2015.
      • D8 - List movie titles together with director names.
      • D9 - Display titles and director names only for movies rated above 8.0.
      • D10 - Show director names alongside their movie titles and IMDb ratings.
      • D11 - Show each genre with the IDs of movies assigned to it.
      • D12 - List all IMDb ratings from the movie table.
      • D13 - List each movie with its director ID.
      • D14 - Show the ID, title, and release year of every movie.
      • D15 - Combine director and actor names.
      • D16 - Find movie IDs that appear both in the movie table and in awards.
      • D17 - Find directors who have not directed any movie yet.
      • D18 - List all movies that have at least one award.
      • D19 - Show movie titles together with each award name they received.
      • D20 - Show every column and row from the movie table.
      • D21 - List all distinct release years present in the movie table.
      • D22 - Find movies with IMDb rating greater than 8.0.
      • D23 - Show all studios with their country information.
      • D24 - Display movie title, release year, IMDb rating, and runtime.
      • D25 - Generate every combination of genres and countries.
      • D26 - List all directors together with their movies, including directors who have no films yet.
      • D27 - Show all movies and all awards including unmatched records from both sides using FULL OUTER JOIN.
      • D28 - Find directors with their average movie rating using a subquery in the FROM clause.
      • D29 - SELECT DISTINCT movie_id, title FROM MOVIE
      • D30 - Group movies by their release year to see which years have films.
      • D31 - Count the number of movies released each year using GROUP BY with aggregate.
      • D32 - Order movies first by year descending, then by rating descending to find best recent films.
      • D33 - Categorize movies by their rating into quality tiers using CASE expression.
      • D34 - Find movies whose title contains a specific word using string pattern matching with LIKE.
      • D35 - Calculate movie age and extract year components from release dates using date functions.
      • D36 - Query the high_rated_movies view to find critically acclaimed films with rating above 8.
      • D37 - List movies and the count of awards they won using a subquery in the SELECT clause.
      • D38 - Insert a new genre named 'Documentary'.
      • D39 - Update the runtime of 'Dune' to 156 minutes.
      • D40 - Delete user ratings that are lower than 2.
      • D41 - List all movies with their award information, keeping rows for movies that have never won.
      • D42 - List movies and the count of awards they won using a subquery in the SELECT clause.
      • D43 - Show movie titles three different ways.
      • D44 - Find genres with more than 2 movies, showing their movie count and average rating, ordered by count.
      • D45 - Query the high_rated_movies view to find critically acclaimed films.
      • D46 - Insert a new genre based on existing data.
      • D47 - Update movie ratings based on subquery.
      • D48 - Delete ratings for movies that don't exist.

    T1 := movie_actor * movie_genre
    T2 := T1[actor_id, genre_id]
    T3 := T2 ÷ genre[genre_id]
    T4 := T3 * actor
    T4[name]
    XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX

    WITH T1 AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT *
        FROM MOVIE_ACTOR
        NATURAL JOIN MOVIE_GENRE
    ),
    T2 AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT actor_id,
                        genre_id
        FROM T1
    ),
    T3 AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT actor_id
        FROM T2
        EXCEPT
        SELECT DISTINCT actor_id
        FROM (
            SELECT DISTINCT *
            FROM (
                SELECT DISTINCT actor_id
                FROM T2
            ) R1
            CROSS JOIN (
                SELECT DISTINCT genre_id
                FROM GENRE
            ) R2
            EXCEPT
            SELECT DISTINCT *
            FROM T2
        ) R3
    ),
    T4 AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT *
        FROM T3
        NATURAL JOIN ACTOR
    )
    SELECT DISTINCT name
    FROM T4;

    SELECT a.name
    FROM actor a
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT g.genre_id
    FROM genre g
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT m.movie_id
    FROM movie m
    JOIN movie_actor ma ON m.movie_id = ma.movie_id
    JOIN movie_genre mg ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id
    WHERE ma.actor_id = a.actor_id
    AND mg.genre_id = g.genre_id
    )
    )
    ORDER BY a.name;
